comments.author: @DanClarkWCP1
comments.text:
I started on my invention idea a few months ago, and just found your videos today. I have to say they have been one of the top 3 or 4 sources of information I've run across, and I've spent a lot of time doing research as well as talking to product design people, tinkerers, patent agents and patent attorneys. I really appreciate the time you've spent to create all these videos. 

Now, when I first heard about the concept of "nonobviousness", at the beginning of this project, I just started shaking my head. It seems so very, very subjective. I like your cookie example, but I have a question, especially about the "elements either known or unknown". Are you saying the commercial baker with two years of experience would have to know about known or unknown elements, and would have to be able to predict or expect a certain result, for the the invention to be obvious?
